title: Stomach polyp removal
what: Through a gastroscope (a thin tube with a camera), the doctor removes a polyp in the stomach with a thin loop or forceps. There are no cuts on your belly.
why: When a polyp was found during gastroscopy and it needs to be removed and examined.
duration: the procedure usually takes 20 to 60 minutes; sometimes you are watched until the evening or overnight in hospital; lab results take 1 to 2 weeks
tell_doctor: Blood thinners - your doctor will tell you what to stop and when
Allergies and any problems with anesthesia

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests for clotting and blood group are usually needed. The clinic will give you the list.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food for 6 to 8 hours. Water is allowed until the time the clinic tells you.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Your doctor will say which to skip.

prepare.title: Companion
prepare.text: After sedation you need someone to go with you.

bring: Your referral and the report from your earlier gastroscopy
steps: A thin tube (catheter) is placed in your vein
You lie on your left side and a mouthguard is placed in your mouth
Sedation is given and you fall asleep
The doctor passes the gastroscope in, finds the polyp and cuts it off with a loop
The spot is sealed with heat or closed with small clips
The polyp is sent to the lab
feel: Under sedation you usually feel nothing and do not remember it
Afterwards you may have a scratchy throat and bloating
Sometimes mild discomfort in the upper belly
after: You start eating at the time your doctor tells you, at first soft, warm food
For a few days eat gentle food, without spicy or hot dishes or alcohol
The doctor may prescribe medicine to protect your stomach
After sedation do not drive for the rest of the day
The lab result comes in 1 to 2 weeks
red_flags: Vomiting blood or something that looks like coffee grounds - call your local emergency number
Black, loose stools with weakness or dizziness - call your local emergency number

faq.a: Most often not. Only the tissue test after removal can say for sure.
Usually not. The stomach has no pain nerves, and the procedure is done under sedation.

reminders.text: Stomach polyp removal tomorrow. Do not eat after dinner. Come in the morning with someone to accompany you.
